posts.title: Tips?
posts.text: Curious how other owners handle tips. About half of my irrigation clients have been tipping for service calls, and I’m wondering how common that is for others. I use Yardbook, which has a built-in tip option for customers when they pay. I’m not actively asking for tips, but the option is there. For context, this is just for my irrigation business, not the lawn maintenance side. How do you handle tipping as an owner? Do you leave the option available, or prefer not to encourage it?

posts.title: Would you trust AI to book your estimates?
posts.text: I've been testing AI phone answering for my brother's landscaping company. Getting it to answer questions is one thing, but letting it put appointments on the calendar is another. There are jobs we don't take, and the last thing I want is an estimate booked for something we don't even do. Would you let AI book estimates, or would you rather have it take the information and call the customer back?

posts.title: What are you running for quote follow-ups and missed calls?
posts.text: hey folks, curious what the room is running these days. im using tradestash for job tracking right now and no complaints there, keeps my crm, quotes, invoices and schedule in one spot which is a big step up from the sticky-note-on-the-dash setup i had before. where im still losing money is two spots it doesnt really cover: follow ups and dealing with missed calls when im on a job. miss two or three a day at times easy and i figure half of those just go call the next guy on the list. what... What are you running for quote follow-ups and missed calls?

posts.title: What do you do when an estimate goes unanswered?
posts.text: Genuine question — I've been talking to a lot of shops lately. You send the quote, hear nothing back. Do you follow up? How many times, and how — call, text, email? Or just move on to the next job? Trying to understand what actually works vs. what everyone means to do but doesn't. What's your process?
